findings.title: Object-literal import() calls still load every app eagerly, so nothing is lazy
findings.body: Each `import("./...")` is a property initializer in the object literal, so every app module is requested as soon as this file is evaluated. Awaiting at the call sites only defers the wait; it does not avoid loading the apps. Deferred loading needs thunks (e.g. `googlecalendar: () => import("./googlecalendar")`) with callers invoking them. The PR description gives no goal, so it is unclear whether the intent was laziness. Also, a module whose import rejects produces an unhandled rejection at load time unless that key is awaited, rather than an error at the lookup site.

findings.title: forEach(async) makes the surrounding try/catch ineffective for calendar errors
findings.body: Before this PR getCalendar was synchronous, so a throw from the CalendarService constructor inside this sync forEach callback reached the try/catch and was logged. Now getCalendar is async: the throw becomes a rejected promise returned by the async callback, which forEach discards. The catch never sees it and it surfaces as an unhandled promise rejection. The deletions are also not awaited, so the function returns true and sends the reschedule email while the old calendar event/meeting is still being deleted. Use for...of with await inside the try.

findings.title: forEach(async) makes the surrounding try/catch ineffective for calendar errors
findings.body: Same change as in the vital reschedule: getCalendar is now async, so errors thrown while creating the calendar service escape the try/catch on line 124-139 and become unhandled rejections. The deleteEvent/deleteMeeting calls are not awaited before the function returns true and sends the reschedule email. Use for...of with await inside the try so failures are logged and ordering is preserved.

findings.title: Async forEach in requestReschedule turns calendar failures into unhandled rejections
findings.body: Previously a synchronous throw from getCalendar inside this forEach propagated and failed the mutation. Now getCalendar is async, so the error is returned from the discarded async callback and becomes an unhandled promise rejection while the mutation reports success. The calendar deleteEvent calls are also not awaited before sendRequestRescheduleEmail runs. Use for...of with await so errors are handled and deletions finish before the email is sent.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes after it has already been awaited
findings.body: The outer `.forEach(async (credential) => ...)` does not return its promise, so the handler continues without waiting for it. The final `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` copies apiDeletes before these callbacks reach their `apiDeletes.push(...)` calls, so these per-occurrence calendar deletions are never awaited. Their results and errors are dropped and failures become unhandled rejections. The PR rewrote the sibling non-recurring loop in the else branch to for...of with await but left this one as forEach(async); it should be converted the same way.

findings.title: `await apiDeletes` awaits an array, not the pending deletions
findings.body: On the paid-cancellation path, `await apiDeletes;` does not wait for the promises inside the array. The handler returns 'Booking successfully cancelled' before calendar and video deletions settle, and their rejections are unhandled. This is pre-existing, but the PR touches these calls and the async change makes the difference observable. Use `await Promise.all(apiDeletes)` if the deletions are meant to complete before responding.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials still calls the now-async getCalendar without await
findings.body: getCalendarCredentials stays synchronous and stores `getCalendar(credential)` directly, so each returned `calendar` field is a Promise<Calendar | null>, not a Calendar. Only getConnectedCalendars currently remembers to await `item.calendar`; any other consumer that uses the field as a Calendar will get undefined methods or a Promise where a value is expected. Make this function async and await the calendar, or document that the field is a Promise.

findings.title: Async conversion changes error propagation in cancel and reschedule paths with no test updates
findings.body: getCalendar, getVideoAdapters, deleteMeeting, deleteEvent and payment app lookup all changed from synchronous to async, and several callers moved from sync forEach to async callbacks. The PR adds no tests or test updates covering what happens when credential or app lookup or CalendarService construction throws during cancel, reschedule, or video deletion. Those error paths are exactly what changed, so they should have coverage.
